flawed_step: Lines 0048-0053 (conclusion of Lemma 1): from |N(S)| <= n-1 and |N(S)| >= n/2 + alpha*n the proof derives alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n and calls this a contradiction for large n. It is the opposite: for any fixed alpha < 1/2 (which line 0019 already established) the inequality alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n HOLDS for all large n, so no contradiction exists. Lemma 1 (delta(G) > alpha*n) is therefore unproved, and in fact false; every later step (lines 0061-0064) depends on it.
counterexample: Take n = 8 and alpha = 1/4. Let V = {v, u1,...,u7}; make {u1,...,u7} a complete graph K_7 and let v be isolated (deg(v) = 0). Expansion check for every S with |S| = n/2 = 4: (a) if v is not in S, S consists of 4 clique vertices, and N(S) = union of (clique minus u_i) over the 4 chosen u_i = all 7 clique vertices, so |N(S)| = 7 >= 4 + 2 = n/2 + alpha*n; (b) if v is in S, S has 3 clique vertices and N(S) = N(v) union N(those 3) = empty union {u1..u7} = 7 >= 6. So G satisfies the hypothesis with alpha = 1/4 > 0, yet delta(G) = deg(v) = 0, which is not > alpha*n = 2. Lemma 1 fails. Plugging this graph into the proof's own construction also breaks the induction: the base case (line 0055) permits choosing v1 = v (any W1 with |W1| >= (1-alpha)n = 6 may contain v, e.g. W1 = {v,u1,u2,u3,u4,u5}), after which N(v1) = empty and line 0062's bound |N(v_i) intersect W_{i+1}| > alpha*n - alpha*n = 0 is false. Also, running the proof's own contradiction computation on this graph with v the isolated vertex gives exactly n/2 + alpha*n = 6 <= n - 1 = 7, confirming that the inequality at line 0050 is satisfiable rather than contradictory.
reasoning_summary: The proof's Lemma 1 derives only alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n from the assumed low-degree vertex, and then misreads this as a contradiction; since line 0019 already showed alpha < 1/2, this inequality is consistent for all large n. A concrete graph (K_7 plus an isolated vertex, n = 8, alpha = 1/4) satisfies the stated expansion hypothesis for every 4-set S while having a degree-0 vertex, refuting Lemma 1 outright. Lemma 1 is the sole justification for the path-extension step (lines 0061-0064), and the same graph makes that step fail when the base case picks the isolated vertex, so the argument as written does not establish the theorem.
